The player is currently at rows 18–23, columns 11–16. The beam is at rows 20–21, columns 16–28 (dashed line). Red is at rows 19–22, columns 42–45. The beam's rows 20–21 overlap with red's rows 19–22.
Next, extend the beam to the right: the beam's end is at column 28. Each RIGHT adds 6: 34, 40, 46. After 3 RIGHTs, the beam's end is at column 46, overlapping with red (columns 42–45). Execute 3 RIGHTs and observe whether red gets collected.
Execute one RIGHT at a time? Or batch all 3? If the beam collects upon contact, then after the 3rd RIGHT the beam's end is at column 46 ≥ 42, so it should be collected. But the beam might stop extending when it hits a block (end at column 41). Either way, after 3 RIGHTs it should be in contact. To be safe, batch the 3 RIGHTs and then check the state.

        bb=n['boundary']; rr=[p[0] for p in bb]; cc=[p[1] for p in bb]
